1.explanation:
1) SkipToContent.js: this component hard-codes inline styles for background and text color; the current blue (rgb(2,122,197))→white ratio (~1.91:1) fails WCAG AA. Adjusting these values or moving to CSS variables that meet a ≥4.5:1 contrast will fix the issue.  
2) HeaderMenuItem.js: by default it renders its <li> with role="menuitem". That is only valid when its ancestors include a role="menubar" or role="menu" container. When users place a HeaderMenuItem inside HeaderGlobalBar (which has no menu role), DAP flags an orphaned menuitem. The default role should be removed or made conditional.  
3) HeaderGlobalBar.js: this container currently has no ARIA role. If the intent is to host menu items, it must declare role="menubar" or role="menu"; otherwise it should forbid rendering children with role="menuitem". Adjusting this file to either apply the correct role or prevent misuse will clear the WAI-ARIA violation.
1.bug_scenario: When running DAP (July 2019 ruleset) against the Header Base w/Navigation or Header Base w/Navigation + Actions UI Shell in Carbon v10 React, two kinds of violations appear: 1) The “Skip to main content” link’s foreground/background contrast (rgb(2,122,197) on white) falls below WCAG AA minimum, and 2) Menu items rendered via <HeaderMenuItem> carry role="menuitem" even when they aren’t inside a parent with role="menu", "menubar", or "group" (for example, when you put them directly in <HeaderGlobalBar>), which violates WAI-ARIA rules.

2.explanation:
1. SkipToContent.js – this file defines the Skip to main content link and hard-codes inline styles that produce a 1.91:1 contrast ratio.  To meet WCAG AA (4.5:1 for normal text), these colors or the way they’re applied need to be adjusted here (or moved into CSS so that themes can override them).

2. HeaderGlobalBar.js – this wrapper renders the container around global header actions (in the narrow viewport example, it holds a HeaderMenuItem).  Because HeaderMenuItem has a default `role="menuitem"`, its immediate ancestor must have an ARIA role of `menu`, `menubar`, or `group`.  We need to update HeaderGlobalBar to apply one of those roles (for example `role="menubar"` or `role="group"`) so that its child menuitems live inside a valid ARIA parent.

3. HeaderMenuItem.js – this component assigns `role="menuitem"` by default to its `<li>`.  If we decide instead to remove or parameterize that default in order to support usage inside HeaderGlobalBar, the change must be made here.  For example, we could change the default prop or make the role conditional.  Any fix around menuitem semantics belongs in this file.
2.bug_scenario:
When we run the DAP accessibility checker on the React Header Base with Navigation (or with Navigation and Actions) UI Shell, we see two categories of violations in the screenshot: 1. Contrast Failure on the “Skip to main content” link: – The link is rendered by the SkipToContent component with inline styles `background-color: #0f62fe` and `color: #ffffff`. DAP reports a contrast ratio of 1.91:1, which fails WCAG AA for 14px / weight 400 text. 2. Invalid ARIA hierarchy on a menu item: – In a narrow viewport, the header navigation collapses to show a menu button and a list of links. A `` renders as `
  • …
    • `, but its parent container does not have one of the allowed ARIA roles (`menu`, `menubar`, or `group`). DAP flags “An element with WAI-ARIA role “menuitem” is not contained in or owned by an element with one of the following WAI-ARIA roles: group, menu, menubar.” Both issues show up under the DAP panel in Chrome DevTools.
